what: The score combines four terms: exact insertion distance, a small nearest-route cohesion penalty, a Clarke–Wright-style bonus for the best still-loadable unassigned partner, and a capacity-packing penalty based on the smallest residual achievable by one additional customer. Packing pressure increases as the route fills. Runtime is O(len(route) + len(unassigned)) per invocation with O(1) extra space.
why: The insertion delta chooses a locally economical slot, while route proximity and depot-relative pair savings favor spatially coherent routes that intra-route 2-opt can subsequently order well. The partner bonus is conditioned on remaining capacity, so attractive geometric pairings that cannot coexist on the route receive no credit. The residual term addresses the substantial capacity pressure and heterogeneous demands seen in the representative instances without solving a knapsack subproblem. This remains a greedy, coefficient-based heuristic: one-step packing can miss multi-customer combinations, pair savings may overemphasize a dense direction, and no improvement is claimed without evaluation on held-out and out-of-family instances.
